extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / specialists in inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and formalizes the reconstruction algorithms and structural definitions used in IUT: mono-anabelian reconstruction of Aut-holomorphic spaces, definitions and reconstructions of log-shells and local log-volume/radial/angular volume functions, and preliminaries on tempered fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: four kinds of objects (étale-like vs Frobenius-like; arith. holomorphic vs mono-analytic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper distinguishes four kinds of objects: arithmetically holomorphic étale-like objects (D), arithmetically holomorphic Frobenius-like objects (F), mono-analytic étale-like objects (D'), and mono-analytic Frobenius-like objects (F').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four types reflect how objects behave under the reconstruction algorithms (relations with X and G_k) and determine which structures (e.g. functoriality, sharing in links, Kummer-detachment) are available. The text repeatedly references this dichotomy when describing which operations (sharing, exchanging, Kummer-isomorphisms) are permissible for each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian Reconstruction (Proposition 4.8) — reconstruct X_v and its Aut-holomorphic structure
rubrics_metrics.description: From the topological group π_1^arith (denoted (π)X) and an Archimedean place v, there is an explicit group-theoretic algorithm (Steps 1–5) to reconstruct the Aut-holomorphic space X_v associated to X_v := X ⊗_k k_v functorially with respect to compatible open injective homomorphisms of profinite groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps summarized: (1) reconstruct NF-points as conjugacy classes of decomposition groups and reconstruct non-constant NF-rational functions and evaluation maps; (2) define Cauchy sequences of NF-points (see separate criterion); (3) build X_top as equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences with topology generated by N(U;f); (4) define local Aut-holomorphic homeomorphism groups Authol(U_v) as maps locally expressible by convergent power series with coefficients in k_v; (5) define AX(UX) and reconstruct the unique Aut-holomorphic structure AX extending the pre-structure. The proposition asserts the correctness and functoriality of these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Cauchy sequence of NF-points (Step 2 of Prop. 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence (x_j)_{j in N} of NF-points is a Cauchy sequence if there exists an exceptional finite set S of NF-points such that x_j ∉ S for all but finitely many j, and for any non-constant NF-rational function f on X_k whose divisor of poles avoids S, the sequence of values f(x_j) in k_v forms a Cauchy sequence in k_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the intrinsic group-theoretic substitute for the usual analytic notion of Cauchy sequence; it is used to form X_top and to extend rational functions by taking limits of their values on representative sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence relation of Cauchy sequences (Step 2 continued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Cauchy sequences (x_j) and (y_j) with a common exceptional set S are equivalent if for every non-constant NF-rational function f on X_k whose divisor of poles avoids S, the sequences f(x_j) and f(y_j) in k_v converge to the same element of k_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence classes of such Cauchy sequences form the points of X_top; the equivalence is tested via convergence of values of all allowable rational functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology on X_top via sets N(U; f) (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open subset U ⊂ k_v and a non-constant NF-rational function f on X_k, N(U; f) is the set of equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences (x_j) with f(x_j) ∈ U for all j. The topology on X_top = X_v(k_v) is generated by these sets N(U; f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the underlying topological space on which Aut-holomorphic structures and extensions of rational functions are defined; non-constant NF-rational functions extend to X_top by taking limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and reconstruction of local Aut-holomorphic groups and AX (Steps 4–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For connected opens U_X ⊂ X_top and U_v ⊂ k_v with a homeomorphism f_U: U_X → U_v induced by a rational function, Authol(U_v) is the group of homeomorphisms of U_v locally expressible as convergent power series with coefficients in k_v. AX(UX) is defined by conjugating Authol(U_v) by f_U, and the unique Aut-holomorphic structure AX on X_top is reconstructed as the extension of the pre-Aut-holomorphic structure given by these groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the criterion for when a topological space obtained from group data carries the required analytic (Aut-holomorphic) structure: the local symmetry groups must be realizable by convergent power series in the local field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of Elliptic Cuspidalisation (Lemma 4.9) — reconstructing AX ≅ k_v
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X elliptically admissible, from π_1^arith and an Archimedean valuation v one can group-theoretically construct an isomorphism AX → k_v of topological fields via an algorithm (Steps 1–3) that reconstructs NF-points, rational functions, evaluation and order maps, E_top and local additive structures and then uses embeddings UX → Hom_{k_v}(𝔪_x/𝔪_x^2, k_v) to assemble the isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm starts locally (reconstructing local additive structures) and then globalizes via compatibility as x varies. The lemma emphasizes the functoriality with respect to compatible homomorphisms of profinite groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell (non-Archimedean) (Definition 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-Archimedean local field k, define k^{(24)} and the p-adic logarithm log_k to transport the topological field structure. Put I_k := (1/(2 p)) · Im( O_k^{(3)} → k^{(24)} )^{(π_1 action) } (notation as in text) and refer to I_k as a Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the arithmetic fundamental group (π)X one can also reconstruct an étale-like holomorphic log-shell I((π)X) using k((π)X) and there is a Kummer isomorphism (Kum (non-Arch)) Ik → I((π)X). These log-shells are central objects used to build log-links and to compare mono-analytic and arithmetically holomorphic pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility inclusions (non-Archimedean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural inclusions used for upper semi-compatibility of log-Kummer correspondence: log_k(O_k^{(2)}) ⊂ I_k and O_k^{(2)}((π)X) ; log_k((π)X)(O_k^{(2)}((π)X)) ⊂ I((π)X), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inclusions express which subdiagrams/subsets can be reconstructed from only mono-analytic data and which require arithmetically holomorphic structure; they are used in proving compatibility properties (e.g., Proposition 13.7(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic reconstruction of log-shell and local log-volume (non-Archimedean) (Proposition 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a topological group G ≅ G_k one can reconstruct group-theoretically: invariants p, f(k), e(k), k^{(24)}, O_k^{(2)}, O_k^{(3)}, the log-shell I(G) (étale-like mono-analytic log-shell), a topological field R_non(G) and a (non-normalised) local log-volume function log(G): M(k^{(24)}(G)^{G}) → R_non(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The local log-volume log(G) is uniquely characterised by three properties: (a) additivity: for disjoint A,B, exp(log(G)(A∪B)) = exp(log(G)(A)) + exp(log(G)(B)); (b) +-translation invariance: log(G)(A+a) = log(G)(A) for a in k^{(24)}(G)^G; (c) normalisation: log(G)(I(G)) = ( (1/(p^?)) + (some expression involving p_G, e_G, f_G, m_G) ) · F(G) (the text gives the precise normalisation formula involving p_G, e_G, f_G, m_G and F(G)). If a field structure on k is given, formula (5.1) relates log(G) to the usual log_k via log(G)(A) = log(G)(log_k(A)) when log_k is bijective on A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark on non-normalisability by OG_k (Remark 5.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cannot normalise log(G) by requiring log(G)(O_G^{k^{(24)}}) = 0 because the subset OG_{k^{(24)}} needs arithmetically holomorphic structure to reconstruct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This points out an obstruction to a natural zero-normalisation in the purely mono-analytic (group-theoretic) reconstruction context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell (Archimedean) (Definition 5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CAF (complex archimedean field) k and an elliptically admissible Aut-holomorphic orbispace X, define the universal cover k^{(24)}, use log_k to transfer topological field structure, and define I_k as the closure of a connected pre-compact open subset (a 'line segment') of k^{(24)} preserved by multiplication by roots of unity and whose endpoints differ by a generator of ker(k^{(24)} → k). I_k is the Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell; similarly one can reconstruct I(X) from X and obtain a Kummer isomorphism Kum (Arch): I_k → I(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction emphasizes that Ik can be defined using only multiplicative/topological group structure of k^{(24)} by taking closures of unions of images under finite-order automorphisms; but to use O_k^{(2)} and the exponential map one needs the topological field structure of k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility inclusions (Archimedean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural inclusions: k^{(24)} ⊃ I_k; O_k^{(2)} ⊃ exp_k(I_k) and similarly for X: O_k^{(3)}(X) ⊃ I(X); O_k^{(2)}(X) ⊃ exp_k(X)(I(X)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inclusions are used to state and prove upper semi-compatibility of log-Kummer correspondences in the Archimedean setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic reconstruction in Archimedean places (Proposition 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a split monoid G ≅ (C^×, C^×)! (notation in text), an algorithm (Steps 1–7) reconstructs: the universal covers C^{(24)}, k^{(24)}(G), the monoid Seg(G) of compact line segments (with monoid structure), a log-shell I(G) inside k^{(24)}(G), an R-module R_arc(G) with distinguished Frobenius element F(G), projections pr_rad and pr_ang and two local (non-normalised) log-volume functions: the local radial log-volume log(G): M(k^{(24)}(G)) → R_arc(G) and the local angular log-volume (ang,rad) log(G): (ang)M(k^{(24)}(G)) → R_arc(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key characterisations: the radial log-volume is obtained by taking the Lebesgue length of the radial projection pr_rad(A) and then logarithm; normalization: log(G)(I(G)) = log( (π?)^{?} ) · F(G) (precise value given in text). The angular log-volume is given by integrating the angular projection pr_ang(A) with the differentiable structure; its normalization on O_k^{(2)}(G) is specified. Relation (5.2) holds: when a field structure and exponential map exp_k are given, log(G)(A) = (ang,rad)log(G)(exp_k(A)) for appropriate A where exp_k induces bijections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to tempered groups and temperoids (Definition 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several foundational definitions: (1) tempered group: topological group expressible as inverse limit of countable discrete groups; (2) temp-slim: tempered group whose open subgroups have trivial centers Z(H) = {1}; (3) relatively temp-slim: relative notion for a homomorphism f: G1 → G2; (4) B_temp(G) and B(G): categories of countable discrete (resp. finite) G-sets; (5) connected temperoid/anabelioid: category equivalent to B_temp(G) (resp. B(G)). Morphisms of temperoids/anabelioids are isomorphism classes of functors preserving finite limits and countable colimits (resp. finite colimits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the categorical and group-theoretic standards by which one builds and recognises tempered fundamental groups, and they justify reconstruction (up to inner automorphism) of the underlying topological group from the category B_temp(G) when G has countable basis (analogous to Galois categories for profinite groups). The text also notes natural bijections among (i) continuous outer homomorphisms G1 → G2, (ii) morphisms B_temp(G1) → B_temp(G2), and (iii) morphisms between the underlying 0-categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic characterisation of geometric vs arithmetic tempered fundamental groups (Lemma 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a hyperbolic curve X over a p-adic field K, the geometric tempered fundamental group (π_1^temp(X ⊗  ar{K})) and the arithmetic tempered fundamental group (π_1^temp(X)) sit in a relation that is characterisable group-theoretically: the homomorphisms to profinite completions are injective, and one can identify the closed subgroup π_1^temp( X ⊗  ar{K}) as the intersection π_1^temp(X) ∩ π_1(X) (as described in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma justifies reconstructing geometric tempered pieces from arithmetic tempered data by purely group-theoretic means; remark notes a pro-(l) analog holds as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of dual semi-graph GX for pointed stable curve (Definition 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Given a pointed stable curve X with marked points D and X := X 
 D, the dual semi-graph G_X is constructed by: vertices = irreducible components of X; closed edges = nodes of X (each closed edge connects the two components meeting at that node); open edges = marked points (each open edge connects to the component containing the marked point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the canonical combinatorial object associated to the special fiber of a stable curve; the construction is used in later arguments about reductions and tempered coverings.
